t.E525.agn: In 1965, JECFA set the ADI for potassium hydroxide as 'not limited'; the evaluation stated that no toxicological reason was seen to limit use in line with good manufacturing practice, but that the total potassium intake from these additives should be kept in mind from a nutritional point of view. In the EU it is a Group I additive; EFSA's re-evaluation has not yet been published (it was included in a call for data in 2016).
t.E525.found.0: May be used at quantum satis (as much as needed) in many foods in the EU
t.E525.found.1: Processed cereal-based foods and baby foods for infants (in the EU only for pH adjustment)
t.E525.prod: It is produced chemically by electrolysis of a potassium chloride solution.
t.E525.regx.1: Group I additive; generally permitted at quantum satis (as much as needed).
t.E525.regx.2: Included in the call for use/concentration data as part of the re-evaluation (deadline 31.01.2017).
t.E525.regx.3: Permitted only for pH adjustment in processed cereal-based foods and baby foods for infants.
t.E525.summary: Potassium hydroxide. Used in cocoa processing and as an acidity regulator.
t.E525.what: It is a strong base (caustic potash) used to regulate acidity and to neutralise. In food it reacts with acids to form potassium salts.
